classification.difficultyReason: Parts a-d require two linked judgements without calculation: the sign of a gives the direction the parabola opens, and the sign of k gives which side of the x-axis the vertex is on. The student then combines these to decide whether the parabola reaches the axis. That is more than reading off a turning point (p17-q5), but each case is routine. Part e is the hardest demand. The student must generalise these case judgements into a symbolic rule ('a and k have opposite signs'), which is a small step of abstraction and reframing. It needs no algebraic solving, no sketching and no multi-step computation. That puts it just below p24-q3, which needs several computed features and a sketch.
